analysis.title: USA: ISM Services Index Declines Slightly; Services PMI Revised Down in Final Reading
key_insights: The ISM services index fell 0.4pt to 54.5 in October, roughly in line with consensus (median forecast 54.8, GS 54.9, prior 54.9).
The ISM services composition was mixed-to-weak. Employment rose 1.3pt to 51.4, while business activity fell 2.7pt to 53.8 and new orders fell 3.9pt to 55.9.
New export orders rebounded 8.3pt to 55.2 after a sharp decline in September.

ISM services prices paid eased 1.0pt to 73.0 after reaching its highest level since July 2022 in September. The press release said tariffs and fuel costs were the most cited issues affecting supply chains, and commentary on supply chain constraints increased significantly since September.

The S&P Global US services PMI was revised down 1.8pt to 56.1 in the October final reading, versus a median forecast of 57.9. New business (-1.5pt to 57.4) and employment (-0.5pt to 53.3) were both revised down.
S&P Global input prices (-1.3pt to 62.1) and output prices (-0.4pt to 58.3) were also revised down in the final reading.
GS reads this week's ISM reports as confirming the broader business survey signal: a healthy pace of activity but no sign of a surge to a far-above-trend pace.
The price components of both ISM surveys eased slightly in October but remain elevated relative to their levels before the start of the Iran war.
